scope: V7-11 JSON chat cancellation and shared JSON/SSE commit semantics
networkScope: Owned loopback HTTP protocol fixture only

priorWindowsFailure.observed: Peer EOF drain returned Windows 10060/TimedOut. Later worker-zero assertion was not reached.

changes: JSON chat now registers task_id, uses the bounded request-owned transport and checks inherited cancellation before egress and the shared commit gate.
JSON HTTP connections use the same scoped peer watcher as completion, so downstream disconnect cancels the owned provider request.
JSON and SSE share the same commit gate: cancellation that wins prevents history persistence; after the gate wins, the atomic complete-turn write finishes even if the downstream disconnects.
The existing seven-key successful JSON envelope remains compatible. JSON aggregation now uses the same strict provider-frame validation as SSE.

receiptSemantics.cancelling: Cancellation was accepted before the commit gate; this is not proof that every worker has already retired.
receiptSemantics.finished: A still-registered task passed the commit gate, so this cancellation lost. A later persistence failure still returns its ordinary failure receipt.
receiptSemantics.unknown: No live cancellation registration was found. This alone proves neither cancellation nor a successful commit; request outcome, history, upstream EOF and worker/slot observations are checked separately.

checks: production CSP and real token; every trailing-slash alias rejects anonymous access before inference; malformed shape makes no provider request
a genuine upstream delta arrives before the fixture is allowed to send the rest; no early history commit, one provider request, exact Unicode and one final usage
nonstream providers emit one genuine delta without a repeated request; the original JSON endpoint remains compatible
bare upstream EOF, malformed frames, invalid UTF-8 and token exhaustion retain partial text without completion, usage or history writes
HTTP 400/403/429 remain distinguishable without echoing provider error bodies, connection or authorization; no successful history
JSON compatibility replies register the same task, stop both JSON and streamed provider reads, retire their slot, and cancel on downstream disconnect without persisting a partial turn
real cancellation before upstream headers and mid-stream responds below 200ms, closes the owned connection below two seconds, preserves history and permits the next request
closing the downstream reader without calling the cancellation route stops the owned upstream request and does not persist a partial answer
incognito replies in both SSE and JSON are usable without raw chat-history persistence; Markdown bytes remain unchanged
a second real process reopens the committed full turn only; failed, cancelled and incognito sessions and BOM/CRLF original remain intact

remaining: The original Windows 10060 failure is still open; no same-candidate Windows or Linux rerun was performed.
The current checks use actual macOS processes and sockets. Native desktop UI, real model/provider inference and OS DNS fault behavior were not certified.

MCP/Extension Host running cancellation was not exercised in this slice; the inherited cancellation check was covered by a Rust unit test. Code-runtime cancellation, managed runtimes and checkpoints retain their separate V7-05 acceptance boundaries.
P1/P2 and V0.0.7 release gates remain open. No commit, push, installation or release was performed.
